tagline: Where the narrow gauge ran, from Dulce up the Navajo River.
intro: This is the New Mexico end of Tracks Across Borders, a 128-mile byway from Chama to Durango that traces the right of way of the abandoned Denver and Rio Grande Western narrow gauge. Out of Chama it heads west into the Jicarilla Apache Nation at Dulce, then turns north past Navajo and up the canyon of the Navajo River to the Colorado line. The road mapped here is only about ten miles of that, out of Dulce and on past Navajo.
Most of the railroad's narrow gauge was abandoned in the 1950s and 1960s. The piece from Antonito to Chama survived as the Cumbres and Toltec. West of Chama the byway keeps to the old line instead.

moments.title: Dulce
moments.text: The Gomez family named their 1877 ranch Agua Dulce for its sweet springs, and it is still theirs, surrounded now by the reservation whose headquarters took the name.

moments.title: Navajo
moments.text: At Navajo the narrow gauge left behind a railroad bridge and a water tank, both well preserved.

moments.title: Navajo River canyon
moments.text: Rock outcrops and tall pines close in along the Navajo River to the Colorado line, on a river whose water goes in large part across the Continental Divide to the Rio Grande.

practical: The stretch up the Navajo River canyon to the Colorado line is not a road to drive in wet or snowy weather.
